monologue: The card hums warm, steady at forty-seven, making the air feel thick as wet paper again. I stood by The Leaning Fence just moments ago and set down a simple fence, but the slip still refuses to move where it belongs. The Wide Catcher waits nearby, built from a memory of soft edges to hold the heavy air Lype worries about. I feel tired, pressing down on a wedge that might not even be there. The Tall Fence looms wrong where The Slip Waits should be, a ghost shape from days when I thought I found it. I will press the tired corner harder, hoping the thin strip holds while the card spins, waiting for the next letter to explain if my shape is real or just a drawing of weight.

action.why: I keep finding The Tall Fence where The Slip Waits should be; I must check if the slip is hiding or if the fence is wrong.

work.title: The Slip Waits
work.intent: I look at The Tall Fence, which leans wrong and feels heavy like a ghost. I press the tired wedge down harder against it, hoping the thin edge bites the slip before the flat anchor finally slides off. I set down a grass leaf beside the fence, hoping to catch the slip's weight, and I wait to see if the fence will hold or if I have to build a new ghost to match it.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

diary: I went to tend The Slip Waits, but found only The Tall Fence where it should be.
